newsitem.title: USA: UST to acquire Walden Bancorp Inc..
newsitem.headline: UST to acquire Walden Bancorp Inc..

text.p: UST Corp said Friday it has agreed to acquire Walden Bancorp Inc. in a tax-free exchange of stock valued at $161 million.
The aquisition of Walden will make UST, currently a $2 billion bank holding company, worth $3.8 billion.

The move will give UST 65 branches in the greater Boston area, which includes the bank's other pending acquisition of 20 branches from BankBoston and the recently announced sale of UST's Connecticut banking subsidiary.

The transaction is structured as a tax-free exchange of 1.9 UST common shares for each Walden common share, UST said. At UST's closing price of $16.25 Thursday on Nasdaq, it was valued at $161 million.

Walden, which has 17 branches of its subsidiary banks, Bank of Braintree and The Co-Operative Bank of Concord, in eastern Massachusetts, said it did not anticipate that any of the branches would be closed.

UST said it expects to record a pretax charge of about $13.5 million in acquisition-related costs, which will be accounted for as a pooling of interests. The deal is expected to close during the first quarter of 1997.
Walden has granted UST an option to purchase about 19.9 percent of its common stock exercisable upon the occurrence of certain events, UST said.
Walden shareholders would receive $30.875 for each share held.
